action_criteria.rationale: Quantifies the executive and social-cognition profile and checks for the slowed processing and motor deficits that would point to HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder.

action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory contributors before attributing decline to neurodegeneration.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Plasma HIV-1 RNA not detected and CD4 count 680 cells/uL
action_criteria.label: Plasma HIV viral load and CD4 count
action_criteria.rationale: Current virological and immune status decides how far HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder and opportunistic infection need pursuing.

action_criteria.label: MRI brain without contrast, dementia protocol
action_criteria.rationale: Shows the lobar frontal atrophy pattern and excludes the white matter disease of HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder, PML and focal opportunistic lesions.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Acellular CSF with normal glucose and undetectable CSF HIV RNA
action_criteria.label: CSF examination with CSF HIV RNA
action_criteria.rationale: In a person with HIV and suppressed plasma viral load, CSF HIV RNA detects CSF viral escape, a treatable cause of new neurocognitive decline; cell count and protein screen for opportunistic infection.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: JC virus PCR not detected; cryptococcal antigen negative
action_criteria.label: CSF JC virus PCR and cryptococcal antigen
action_criteria.rationale: Optional here: with a CD4 count of 680 cells/uL and normal white matter on MRI, PML and cryptococcal disease are very unlikely.

action_criteria.label: FDG-PET when the structural picture is unresolved
action_criteria.rationale: Frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism with posterior sparing supports FTD over AD.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
Do not stop or interrupt antiretroviral therapy.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state the features present (disinhibition, loss of empathy, compulsive and stereotyped behaviour, executive-predominant neuropsychological profile), the functional decline (loss of work), and the level of certainty (probable, given the frontal atrophy).

Explain why HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder, CSF viral escape, opportunistic infection and treatment-resistant depression do not account for the syndrome: suppressed plasma and CSF HIV RNA, CD4 680, normal white matter, a cortical frontal rather than subcortical profile, and a change unlike her earlier depressive episodes.
Continue Biktarvy without interruption, inform her HIV physician of the diagnosis, and check any new psychotropic against the antiretroviral regimen.
Address safety and capacity: driving, finances (giving away possessions), fitness to practise and her clients' safety at work, and vulnerability from sexual disinhibition.
Arrange support and education for her friend and family, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.
Offer genetic counselling before any genetic test, given onset at 54 and a maternal aunt with dementia from her late 50s.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET or perfusion SPECT is the functional study when one is needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

results.finding: Three of six core features within the first three years define possible bvFTD. Probable bvFTD requires functional decline and supportive imaging.
results.source: Rascovsky K et al. Brain 2011;134:2456-2477 (FTDC criteria for bvFTD)

results.finding: Primary psychiatric disorders are the commonest misdiagnosis. No disease-modifying treatment is available.

behavioural variant frontotemporal demen.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. Psychiatric disorders are the main mimics and are excluded on course and examination rather than on a single test. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

Optional: FDG-PET or perfusion SPECT, CSF JCV/cryptococcal antigen, counselled genetic testing, literature. Recommended: antiretroviral interaction review.
key_educational_points: Genetic testing is optional after counselling and is not required to diagnose the clinical FTD syndrome
metadata.notes: Moderate bvFTD in a woman with well-controlled HIV. Teaching: in suppressed HIV, CSF HIV RNA is measured to exclude CSF viral escape; JCV PCR and cryptococcal antigen are optional when the CD4 count is high and the white matter is normal. HAND is subcortical; this syndrome is frontal and behavioural. Antiretroviral therapy continues without interruption.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. J is a 55-year-old clinical social worker with HIV (on Biktarvy for 8 years), hypertension, and depression who is referred from her psychiatrist for neurological evaluation. She presents with her close friend of 20 years, who serves as the primary informant. Her psychiatrist referred her after 15 months of progressive behavioral and personality changes that have not responded to two antidepressant trials (escitalopram and now sertraline at 150 mg). Her friend describes a 15-month history of progressive behavioral changes that are markedly different from her previously known depressive episodes. She has become impulsive — she gave away her laptop to a stranger on the street, claiming he 'needed it more.' She made sexually inappropriate comments to a colleague at work, leading to an HR complaint, which she dismissed entirely. She now follows a rigid daily schedule of her own design and becomes agitated when anything deviates from it. She has developed a habit of watching the same nature documentary series every evening, having watched each episode more than 30 times. She shows no empathy toward clients, which her supervisor noted in an incident report — she was asking detailed questions about clients' trauma histories in front of other staff. She is on medical leave from work. She has no insight into these changes. Her HIV clinic has recorded an undetectable plasma viral load at every visit for the past 6 years. The change began in her mid-50s and has progressed despite the two antidepressant trials.
